Does Universe OS support Secure Boot?

Partially. The EFI image carries the Microsoft+Canonical dual-signed shim and Canonical-signed GRUB, so the boot menu loads and renders. The mainline kernel is not signed, so actually booting with Secure Boot ON is blocked by firmware. To boot Universe OS on a Secure Boot machine, turn Secure Boot off — or sign the kernel in a future release.

What is universe-privilege?

universe-privilege is the privilege gate — and it literally IS sudo: /usr/bin/sudo is a symlink to it. Every root request opens a GUI consent dialog that names the app, the permission category and the exact command, highlights dangerous ones in red, and offers grant durations: just once, this session, 5 minutes, 30 minutes or 1 hour. With no display it denies by default, and it auto-denies after 45 seconds.

How does sudo work in Universe OS?

sudo is a symlink to universe-privilege, so every root request opens the graphical consent gate instead of a terminal password prompt. Approved commands are executed by the setuid gate-exec helper from a single-use job file — the only line in sudoers is: universe ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/lib/universe/gate-exec.

What is gate-exec?

gate-exec is the ONLY custom setuid-root binary (written in C). Approved commands are deposited as single-use tokens into /var/lib/universe/approved (mode 0700), and gate-exec executes them with a minimal environment allowlist, deleting the token before running. It is the single narrow door through which root actions pass.

Check in this order: Watch the kernel as you plug it in (`dmesg -w  (plug the device, watch the lines)`) -> List USB devices to confirm it enumerated (`lsusb`) -> List block devices to see if a disk appeared (`lsblk -f`) -> Check for filesystem support messages (`dmesg -T | grep -iE 'exfat|ntfs|sdb' | tail`) -> Try another port and cable (`physical swap - no command for this one`). Fix: If lsusb shows it but lsblk does not, it is a storage/mode problem. If it appears in lsblk, mount it (or install exfatprogs/ntfs-3g for the filesystem).
